instruments.name: Piano
instruments.description: Our piano program builds strong basics. Students learn hand position, rhythm, music reading, and song practice.
instruments.recommendedAge: around age 5 or 6, depending on attention span and readiness

FAQs.q: What age can kids start piano lessons?
FAQs.a: Most children can begin piano lessons around age 5 or 6, depending on attention span and readiness.

FAQs.q: Are private piano lessons better for kids?
FAQs.a: Yes. Private lessons allow instructors to tailor lessons specifically to your child's pace and learning needs.

FAQs.q: Does my child need a piano at home?
FAQs.a: A keyboard is enough to start. Your instructor can recommend equipment as lessons progress.

FAQs.q: How often should kids take piano lessons?
FAQs.a: One lesson per week is ideal for steady progress and skill development.

FAQs.q: Do you teach beginners?
FAQs.a: Absolutely. Our piano program is beginner-friendly and designed for first-time students.

crossCuttingFindings.lessonFormatContradiction: Five instrument pages state ALL lessons in that instrument are private (guitar, violin, singing explicitly; piano, drums, bass, ukulele implicitly). /group-music-lessons/, /band-builders/, /programs/ and try.southdademusic.com all sell group instruction in the same instruments. /resources/ states the standard offer is 'two classes weekly: one for skill, one for band application'. These cannot all be true.
crossCuttingFindings.frequencyContradiction: Every instrument page says one lesson per week. /resources/ says two classes weekly. Unresolved.
crossCuttingFindings.pricingAbsent: No instrument page states any price, lesson length, or package structure. Lesson duration (30/45/60 min) is never mentioned anywhere on the site.
crossCuttingFindings.scholarshipAbsent: No instrument page mentions PEP/UA eligibility.
crossCuttingFindings.guaranteeAbsent: No instrument page mentions the Stage-Ready Guarantee or the 90-day promise.
crossCuttingFindings.deadCTAPattern: Five instrument pages end with an emoji contact block ('Contact us to schedule a lesson', 'Visit our South Dade studio', 'Explore all music programs online') rendered as plain text with no links. Every instrument page loses the visitor at the bottom of the funnel.
